the dsh-change-review Skill that teaches an agent what a rejected change means.
# @moazzamak/dsh-code-review
A code-review pack for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`). It adds a `/review` command that opens the newest t
urn's changed files, compared one by one, and a Skill that tells the agent what that record covers a
nd how to keep a turn cheap to review.
> **Unofficial community pack.** Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or published by DeepSeek. See Nam
ing and affiliation.
English | 中文
## Which dsh this drives
DeepSeek Harness replaced its review surface in the 0.2 line, and this pack follows it.
| Pack | dsh | What `/review` opens |
| 0.2.x | 0.2 and later | The selected turn's **changed files**, each with a side-by-side or unified

comparison. There is no keep/reject step. |
| 0.1.x | 0.1.5 | The pinned **Changes** page, with per
-chunk Keep/Reject that reverted a rejected chunk in the working tree. |
dsh 0.2 removed the keep/reject surface entirely: nothing reverts a change behind the agent's back a
ny more, no rejection is reported back to the model, and the diff record is read-only. The 0.2 Skill
says so, because an agent told to expect a rejection note would wait for one that never arrives. Us
e 0.1.x only on a dsh 0.1.5 build.

Once installed, three things appear: a **Plugins** entry in Settings, `/review` in the input, and `d
sh-change-review` in the agent's Skill list.
### Desktop app
The Electron desktop build runs the same dsh surfaces, so the comparison view is there without any p
lugin. Adding *this pack* to a packaged desktop app is a separate step: the app's **Desktop Plugins*
* window installs plugins into its own profile with its bundled pnpm, and it accepts npm registry sp
ecs only. Add the bundle to that profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list, or install it from a local ch
y. Add the bundle to that profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list, or install it from a local checkout.
## What you get
- **`/review`** — opens the newest recorded turn's changed files in the right sidebar. Each row is o
ne file; opening it shows that file's turn-start and turn-end contents as hunks, side by side or uni
fied, with line wrapping. `/review` appears only while all three of these hold: the comparison view
is registered, the Session's right column is mounted, and the Session has a turn whose changes were
recorded. A command whose page has nowhere to open is worse than an absent command, so the pack hide

s it rather than offering a no-op.
- **The `dsh-change-review` Skill** — what the agent cannot learn
from a tool result: that a turn, not a tool call, is the unit you review; that only top-level turns
are recorded, so a subagent's edits are never in your diff; that a Session reopened after a Host re
start has no comparison for its earlier turns; and that nothing is reverted, so a comment on a chang

e means the change is still in the file.
- **Precedence over the built-in diff card** — while the pa
ck is installed, dsh's own changed-files card no longer appears under each turn, so `/review` is the
way into a turn's changes rather than one of two. See Precedence for the one case the pack leaves a
into a turn's changes rather than one of two. See Precedence for the one case the pack leaves alone.
The recording, the comparison, and the turn-tail card are part of dsh itself. This pack adds the sho
rtcut, the instructions, and the precedence, nothing else.
## Precedence
`/review` opens dsh's own per-file comparison; it is the built-in diff view, reached by shortcut. So
"the pack takes precedence" cannot mean a different viewer — it means dsh stops offering its **seco
nd** way in. That second way is the changed-files card dsh draws under each completed turn, whose he
ader opens the same comparison.
While the pack is installed, that card is suppressed: the transcript goes back to prose plus tool ro
ws, and the diff surface lives in the right sidebar, where `/review` puts it.
Two limits are deliberate.
- **A turn that declared files with the `present` tool keeps the built-in card.** The card and the d
eclared-file rows are drawn by one component, and this pack has no substitute for the rows, so suppr
essing the card there would delete the rows with it. The pack claims a turn only while the card is t

he only thing that component would draw.
- **Precedence is the pack's, not a preference.** There is
nothing to switch on and no setting it reads or changes; removing the pack restores the card.
The pack does not read or change **Show coding view** (`developerTools`) — the setting described und
er The turn-tail card — and turning that setting off still removes the card the ordinary way, whethe
r or not this pack is installed.
## Requirements
The pack drives dsh's own review surface, so it needs a dsh build that includes it:
| What it uses | Package |
| The comparison view and the `changes-review` tab kind | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-deliverables`

|
| The closing-turn chain the built-in diff card is contributed to | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-ch

at` |
| The slot renderer the suppression contributes through | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer

` |
| `openResource`, and the mounted-Session snapshot | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right`

|
| The Session's loaded event window (`sessions.binding`) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controlle

r` |
| The `workspace/changes` event that names each recorded turn | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace-cha

nges` |
| A Skill registry | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill` |
The tab kind, the chain key, the event, and the address format it opens are private to those package
s, so this pack restates them in one module (`src/protocol.ts`) and pins each restated fact with a t
est. A dsh build that renames the kind, the chain, the event, or the address fails that test rather
than silently breaking `/review` — or silently losing the precedence, which would put the card back
without anyone noticing.
Every dsh package is declared as an optional peer, so installing the pack never pulls a second copy
